ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is a certain mass of carbon dioxide in a sealed container. When the volume $V$ (in $m^3$) of the container changes, the density $\rho$ (in $kg/m^3$) of the gas changes accordingly. It is known that the density $\rho$ and the volume $V$ have an inverse proportional function relationship. The graph of this relationship is shown in the figure. When $V=5m^3$, $\rho=1.98kg/m^3$. Find the analytic formula of the density $\rho$ as a function of the volume $V$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since density $\rho$ is inversely proportional to volume $V$,\\
we set $\rho=\frac{k}{V}\left(V>0\right)$.\\
Given $V=5\mathrm{m}^3$ and $\rho=1.98\mathrm{kg/m}^3$,\\
hence $1.98=\frac{k}{5}$,\\
thus $k=1.98\times 5=9.9$.\\
Therefore, the formula relating density $\rho$ to volume $V$ is: \boxed{\rho=\frac{9.9}{V}\left(V>0\right)}
